original_value: A vine copula model is a flexible high-dimensional dependence model which uses only bivariate building blocks. However, the number of possible configurations of a vine copula grows exponentially as the number of variables increases, making model selection a major challenge in development. In this work, we formulate a vine structure learning problem with both vector and reinforcement learning representation. We use neural network to find the embeddings for the best possible vine model and generate a structure. Throughout experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we show that our proposed approach fits the data better in terms of loglikelihood. Moreover, we demonstrate that the model is able to generate high-quality samples in a variety of applications, making it a good candidate for synthetic data generation.

result.paraphrase: A vine copula model is a flexible, high-dimensional dependence framework built from bivariate components only. Yet as the number of variables grows, the set of possible vine configurations expands exponentially, so selecting a model becomes a major development challenge. In this study, we cast vine structure learning as a problem using both vector and reinforcement learning representations. A neural network is used to learn embeddings for the best vine model and to produce a structure. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that the proposed method fits the data better by loglikelihood. We also show that the model can generate high-quality samples across a range of applications, making it a strong candidate for synthetic data generation.
